name: Cockroaches
metaDescription: Cockroach control in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices. How treatment works, what affects the price, and how to prepare.
summary: Inspection and treatment for cockroaches in homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: Seeing the odd cockroach in a Singapore home isn't unusual: they come in through floor traps, pipes and the gap under the main door, especially after heavy rain. Seeing them regularly, or seeing small ones in the kitchen during the day, usually means they're living and breeding indoors, and a supermarket spray won't reach where they hide.
Tell us about the problem and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm. The firm inspects, explains what it has found, quotes, and carries out the treatment.
signs: Small light-brown cockroaches, often with two dark stripes behind the head, in the kitchen, around the fridge and stove or inside cabinets. These are usually German cockroaches, which breed indoors.
Large reddish-brown cockroaches coming up through floor traps, bathroom drains or from the refuse chute area. These are usually American cockroaches, which live in drains and sewers.
Cockroaches out in daylight. They hide during the day, so seeing them then often points to a larger population.
Droppings like ground pepper or coffee grounds along cabinet hinges, drawer corners and behind appliances.
Egg cases, small brown capsules, tucked into cracks, behind appliances or inside cabinets.
A musty, oily smell in the cupboards where they hide.
signsNote: The species matters because it changes the treatment. The firm will usually ask how big they are and where you see them, so a photo helps.

treatments.name: Gel baiting
treatments.body: Small dots of bait gel go into cracks, hinges and the gaps behind appliances, where cockroaches hide. They eat it and carry it back to the others. It's the usual first choice for German cockroaches in kitchens, because it goes where they live and leaves little on open surfaces.

treatments.name: Residual spraying
treatments.body: An insecticide is sprayed along skirting, drains, floor traps and entry points, and keeps working for a period after it dries. It's commonly used against the larger drain cockroaches and around the outside of landed homes.

treatments.name: Dusting and crack treatment
treatments.body: Insecticide dust is puffed into wall voids, electrical trunking and gaps that sprays and gels can't reach.

treatments.name: Insect growth regulators
treatments.body: These products stop young cockroaches developing into breeding adults. They're often combined with baiting to break the breeding cycle.

treatments.name: Follow-up visits
treatments.body: An established indoor population rarely clears in one visit, because eggs protected in their cases survive the first treatment. Firms commonly schedule one or more follow-ups a few weeks apart, and offices often move onto a regular service.

treatmentNote: Which combination you get depends on the species, how established they are and what the firm finds. Ask what products will be used and where, and whether any area needs to be kept clear afterwards.
priceFactors: How established the problem is: a few drain cockroaches wandering in is a different job from a breeding population in the kitchen.
The size of the property, and how many rooms or areas need treating.
The species, which decides the method.
How many visits are needed, and whether follow-ups are included in the quote.
Whether it's a one-off treatment or a regular service, which is common for offices.
Access: treating after office hours or at weekends, or working around a fully fitted kitchen.
prepare: Clear the kitchen counters and be ready to empty the cabinets under the sink and around the stove, so the firm can reach cracks and hinges.
Put food, utensils and pet bowls in sealed containers or away from the areas to be treated.
Don't use your own insecticide spray in the days before a baiting treatment. Sprays can put cockroaches off the bait.
Note where and when you see them, and take a photo if you can.
Plan for children and pets to stay away from treated areas for as long as the firm advises.
onTheDay: The firm inspects first: kitchen, bathrooms, floor traps, behind appliances and anywhere else you've mentioned.
It explains what it found and which treatment it proposes, if that wasn't settled in the quote.
Treatment is applied. Baiting is quiet and quick; spraying may mean keeping out of a room for a while.
Before leaving, the firm tells you how long to stay clear of treated areas, what not to wipe down, and when any follow-up is due.
afterwards: It's normal to see more cockroaches for a few days after treatment, as they come out of hiding. Don't wipe away the bait, fix any dripping taps, and keep food sealed and the bin covered, because food and water are what drew them in.

premises.hdb: In HDB flats, cockroaches often travel between units through the shared drainage stacks, floor traps and the refuse chute area, so a flat can be reinfested from next door. Treatment focuses on the kitchen and bathrooms, and floor-trap covers or sealing gaps around pipes help keep drain cockroaches out. If neighbours have the same problem, tell the town council, which looks after the common areas.
premises.condo: In a condo, your unit is yours to treat, while the common areas, bin centre and drains are the management corporation's. If you're seeing large drain cockroaches, ask the managing agent whether common-area treatment is scheduled, so the two work together.
premises.landed: Landed homes have more ways in: perimeter drains, the garden, the roof space and usually a larger kitchen and service yard. Treatment normally covers the outside and the drains as well as the inside, and it's more often set up as a regular service.
premises.office: Offices usually find cockroaches in pantries, near bins and in ceiling spaces. Treatment can normally be done out of hours, so no one has to work around it. Check with building management first: it may already have a firm treating the common areas.

faqs.q: Is cockroach treatment safe with children and pets?
faqs.a: Gel baits go into cracks rather than onto open surfaces, and the firm will tell you how long to keep children and pets away from anything sprayed. Tell the firm in advance about babies, pets or anyone with asthma, so it can choose the method to suit.

faqs.q: Why am I seeing more cockroaches after treatment?
faqs.a: Bait and residual treatments take time, and affected cockroaches often come out into the open for a few days. Eggs laid before the treatment can also hatch later, which is why follow-up visits are common. If you're still seeing many after the period the firm gave you, tell it.

faqs.q: Can I just use a supermarket spray?
faqs.a: For the odd cockroach that wanders in from a drain, a spray may be all you need. For a breeding population in the kitchen, sprays usually miss the cracks where they live and can scatter them into other rooms. That's usually the point to get an inspection.

name: Termites
metaDescription: Termite inspection and treatment in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices: baiting, soil treatment and what affects the price.
summary: Termite inspection and treatment for homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: Termites do their damage out of sight, inside door frames, skirting, built-in wardrobes and flooring, so by the time you notice them the colony is often well established. They're one pest where waiting to see whether it goes away usually makes the job bigger.
Tell us what you've found and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm. The firm inspects, works out which kind of termite it is and how far it has spread, and quotes the treatment.
signs: Mud tubes: thin tunnels of soil running up walls, along skirting, or from the floor into door frames and cabinets. Subterranean termites build them to travel between the soil and the wood they're eating.
Wood that sounds hollow when tapped, or crumbles or gives when pressed, especially door frames, skirting and the base of built-in wardrobes.
Bubbling or blistered paint, or wallpaper that ripples, where termites are feeding behind it.
Swarms of winged insects indoors, often around lights in the evening, followed by little piles of shed wings on windowsills and floors.
Small heaps of tiny pellets, like fine sand, below wooden furniture or frames. This points to drywood termites, which live inside the wood itself.
Doors or drawers that suddenly start to stick because the frame has been weakened.
signsNote: Flying ants swarm too. Termites have straight antennae, a thick waist and two pairs of wings of equal length; flying ants have bent antennae and a pinched waist. A photo helps the firm tell them apart.

treatments.name: Inspection
treatments.body: Every termite job starts here: finding where they are, how they're getting in, and whether they're subterranean termites coming from the soil or drywood termites living in the wood. The treatment depends on the answer.

treatments.name: Baiting systems
treatments.body: Bait stations go onto active mud tubes indoors, or into the ground around a landed property. Termites feed on the bait and carry it back to the colony, which is gradually wiped out. It works slowly, with regular checks over weeks or months, but it aims at the colony rather than only the termites you can see.

treatments.name: Liquid soil treatment
treatments.body: A termiticide is applied to the soil around and under a building, creating a treated zone termites can't cross. It's mainly used for landed homes and ground-floor premises, and sometimes means drilling small holes through the floor slab to reach the soil beneath.

treatments.name: Direct wood treatment
treatments.body: Termiticide foam, dust or liquid is injected into infested frames and furniture. It's the usual method for drywood termites and for localised activity, often alongside baiting.

treatments.name: Pre-construction and renovation treatment
treatments.body: Soil treatment before a new slab is laid, or treatment of timber during a renovation, protects the building from the start. It's worth asking about before any major works on a landed home.

treatmentNote: Termite work often comes as a programme of visits rather than a single treatment. Ask what happens if activity returns, whether there's a warranty and how long it lasts, and which inspections are included.
priceFactors: Whether they're subterranean or drywood termites, which decides the method.
How far the activity has spread: one door frame, or several rooms and built-in carpentry.
The method. Baiting runs over several visits, while soil treatment depends on the building's footprint and whether drilling is needed.
The size and type of property. A landed house with a garden is treated very differently from a flat on a high floor.
How long any monitoring or warranty period runs, and how many inspections it includes.
Whether damaged wood needs replacing. That's carpentry, usually quoted separately.
prepare: Leave mud tubes and damaged wood as they are. Breaking them open or spraying them can drive termites into another part of the home.
Clear access to the affected areas: the inside of built-in wardrobes, the space under kitchen cabinets and the skirting behind furniture.
Note every spot where you've seen signs, including the ones that seem minor.
For landed homes, make sure the firm can reach the outside walls, garden beds and any timber in the garden.
If you're renovating, tell the firm and your contractor before damaged carpentry is torn out.
onTheDay: The firm inspects the affected areas and the rest of the property, looking for mud tubes, damaged wood and the likely way in.
It confirms the type of termite and recommends a method.
For baiting, stations are fitted over active areas and dates are set to check and refill them.
For soil treatment, the firm works around the building and, where needed, drills and injects through the floor slab, then patches the holes.
Before leaving, it tells you what to leave alone and which signs to report between visits.
afterwards: Don't move bait stations or clear away mud tubes the firm has baited. Cut down what attracts termites: fix leaks, keep timber and cardboard off damp floors, and in landed homes keep soil and garden mulch away from wooden structures.

premises.hdb: HDB flats get termites too, including on high floors, where they can come in through cracks, service ducts and wooden fittings brought in from outside. Activity usually shows up in door frames, skirting and built-in carpentry. Baiting and direct treatment are the usual methods, because soil treatment isn't practical above the ground floor.
premises.condo: In a condo, termites inside your unit are yours to treat, but if the activity seems to be coming from the structure, the landscaping or several units, tell the managing agent. The management corporation may need to treat the common property, and treating only your unit won't stop them coming back.
premises.landed: Landed homes are the most exposed: the house sits on soil and often has a garden, timber decking and older wooden fittings. Firms commonly propose soil treatment or ground baiting around the house, together with a programme of inspections.
premises.office: In offices, termites tend to turn up in carpentry, raised flooring, partition walls and document storage. The firm can usually work out of hours. If you lease the space, tell building management, because the source may be in the structure or in another tenant's unit.

faqs.q: Can I get rid of termites myself?
faqs.a: Spraying the termites you can see kills only those termites, and often drives the rest of the colony into another part of the home. Professional treatment aims to reach the colony itself, which is why an inspection comes first.

faqs.q: How long does termite treatment take?
faqs.a: It depends on the method. Direct treatment and soil treatment are done in one visit or a few, while baiting works gradually and is checked over a series of visits until the activity stops. The firm will set out its schedule in the quote.

faqs.q: Do flying termites mean I have an infestation?
faqs.a: A few winged termites near a light can come in from outside. Swarms indoors, or shed wings piling up on windowsills, suggest a colony may be close by, and that's worth an inspection.

name: Bed bugs
metaTitle: Bed Bug Treatment Singapore | Homes & Offices
metaDescription: Bed bug treatment in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices: the signs, treatment options, how to prepare and what affects the price.
summary: Bed bug inspection and treatment for homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: Bed bugs aren't a sign of a dirty home. They travel in luggage, bags and second-hand furniture, hide in the seams of mattresses, bed frames and sofas, and come out at night to feed. They're hard to clear with home remedies because they hide so well, and because their eggs survive treatments that kill the adults.
Tell us what you've found and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm, which inspects, confirms whether it's bed bugs, and quotes the treatment.
signs: Itchy bites in lines or clusters, often on the arms, neck and shoulders, that appear after sleeping. Bites alone don't prove it's bed bugs: people react differently, and other insects bite too.
Small dark spots, like dots from a marker pen, on mattress seams, sheets and the bed frame. These are droppings.
Tiny smears of blood on sheets or pillowcases.
Live bugs: flat, oval, reddish-brown and about the size of an apple seed, in mattress seams, bed-frame joints, headboards and sofa cushions.
Pale shed skins and tiny white eggs in the same hiding places.
A sweet, musty smell in badly affected rooms.
signsNote: Check the seams and corners of the mattress, the joints of the bed frame and behind the headboard with a torch. If you catch one, stick it to a piece of tape or seal it in a bag so the firm can identify it.

treatments.name: Inspection
treatments.body: The firm checks beds, sofas, bedside furniture, curtains and nearby cracks to confirm it's bed bugs and to find out how many rooms are affected. Treating only the bed often isn't enough.

treatments.name: Residual insecticide treatment
treatments.body: Insecticide is applied to seams, frames, joints, skirting and the cracks where bed bugs hide. Because eggs aren't reliably killed, a second treatment is commonly booked about two weeks later to catch the newly hatched bugs.

treatments.name: Steam treatment
treatments.body: High-temperature steam on mattresses, sofas and fabrics kills bed bugs and their eggs on contact, without chemicals. It's often combined with insecticide for hiding places steam can't reach.

treatments.name: Mattress encasements
treatments.body: Sealed covers trap any bed bugs left inside a mattress and make new ones easy to spot. They support treatment; they don't replace it.

treatments.name: Removing badly infested items
treatments.body: Sometimes the practical answer is to get rid of a heavily infested mattress or sofa. It needs to be wrapped and sealed before it's moved, so it doesn't drop bugs on the way out.

treatmentNote: Ask how many visits are included, what you need to do between them, and whether a final inspection is part of the quote.
priceFactors: How many rooms are affected, and how many beds, sofas and other pieces of furniture need treating.
How long the problem has been going on, which affects how far the bugs have spread.
The method: insecticide, steam, or both.
The number of visits. Bed bug treatment is usually more than one.
Clutter around beds and sofas, which adds hiding places and time.
For offices, the number of workstations, meeting rooms and upholstered chairs involved.
prepare: Follow the firm's preparation list closely. Bed bug treatment depends on it more than most pest treatments do.
Wash bedding, curtains and clothes from the affected rooms on a hot cycle and tumble-dry them on high heat, then keep them in sealed bags until after treatment.
Clear the floor and the space under the bed, and empty bedside drawers, so the firm can reach every hiding place.
Don't move furniture, bedding or belongings out of affected rooms into other rooms. That's how bed bugs spread through a home.
Don't use your own sprays or foggers beforehand. They can drive bed bugs into walls and other rooms.
Don't throw out a mattress or sofa until the firm has seen it. It may be treatable, and if it isn't, it needs wrapping before it's moved.
onTheDay: The firm inspects beds, sofas and nearby furniture, and confirms which rooms need treating.
Mattresses, frames, sofas, skirting and cracks are treated with insecticide, steam, or both.
You'll be asked to keep out of treated rooms for a few hours, or as long as the firm advises, and to let surfaces dry before using them.
Before leaving, the firm books the follow-up visit and tells you what to do in the meantime.
afterwards: Keep sleeping in your own bed after treatment; moving to another room can lead the bugs there. Vacuum around the bed often, keep bags and luggage off the bed, and check luggage and second-hand furniture after you bring them home. Report any new bites or signs before the follow-up visit.

premises.hdb: In HDB flats, bed bugs usually arrive in luggage, second-hand furniture or with visitors, and in a compact layout they spread between rooms quickly. Treatment usually covers every bedroom and the living-room sofa, not only the room where the bites started.
premises.condo: In a condo, it's usually a treatment for your own unit. If you let the unit out, or a tenant has just moved in or out, deal with it before the next person moves in: bed bugs can survive a long time in an empty unit.
premises.landed: Landed homes have more bedrooms and usually more furniture, so it's important to inspect every room where people sleep or sit. Check the helper's room, guest rooms and rooms that are rarely used, too.
premises.office: Bed bugs in offices usually arrive in bags and clothing, and hide in upholstered chairs, breakout sofas and around workstations. The firm can treat out of hours or over a weekend. It also helps to tell staff what to check at home, so the problem doesn't keep coming back.

faqs.q: How many treatments do bed bugs need?
faqs.a: Usually more than one. Insecticides don't reliably kill eggs, so a follow-up visit is commonly booked to catch bed bugs that hatch after the first treatment. The firm will confirm the number of visits in its quote.

faqs.q: Do I need to throw out my mattress?
faqs.a: Not always. Many mattresses can be treated and then sealed in an encasement. If one is too badly infested, the firm will say so, and it should be wrapped and sealed before it leaves the room.

faqs.q: Can bed bugs spread to my neighbours?
faqs.a: They can, especially in flats, through gaps around pipes and wiring and on people's belongings. That's another reason not to put off treatment.

name: Rodents
metaTitle: Rat & Rodent Control Singapore | Homes & Offices
metaDescription: Rat and mouse control in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices: the signs, baiting and proofing, and what affects the price.
h1: Rat and rodent control in Singapore
summary: Rat and mouse inspection, control and proofing for homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: Rats and mice spoil food, gnaw through wiring and pipes, and can carry disease, so one in the home or office is worth dealing with quickly. Most jobs have two halves: removing the rodents that are there, and closing the gaps they used to get in.
Tell us what you've seen or heard and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm. The firm inspects, finds the way in, and quotes for control and proofing.
signs: Droppings: dark and pellet-shaped, along walls, in cabinets, behind appliances or in the false ceiling. Rat droppings are bigger than a grain of rice; mouse droppings are smaller.
Scratching or scurrying in the ceiling, the walls or behind kitchen cabinets, usually at night.
Gnaw marks on food packaging, cables, doors, plastic pipes and furniture.
Dark, greasy rub marks along skirting and walls, where rodents run the same route again and again.
Burrows in garden beds or along drains and walls outside landed homes.
Nests of shredded paper, fabric or insulation in storerooms, ceilings and behind appliances.
A strong, stale smell in enclosed spaces.
signsNote: The rodents found in Singapore homes are usually rats: the larger brown rat, which lives in drains and at ground level, and the roof rat, which climbs pipes, trees and cables into ceilings. House mice turn up too. Where the signs are tells the firm which one it's dealing with.

treatments.name: Inspection and entry-point survey
treatments.body: The firm finds where rodents are getting in, where they travel and where they nest. Common ways in are gaps around pipes and cables, drains, the gap under doors, roof eaves and false ceilings.

treatments.name: Baiting
treatments.body: Rodent bait goes into locked, tamper-resistant stations along the routes rodents use, out of reach of children and pets. The firm checks and replaces the bait over several visits until activity stops.

treatments.name: Trapping
treatments.body: Traps are used where bait isn't suitable, such as kitchens and homes with pets, or to catch a rodent quickly. The firm removes whatever is caught on its visits.

treatments.name: Proofing
treatments.body: Entry points are sealed with wire mesh, metal plates, sealant and door brushes so rodents can't come back. Without proofing, new rodents often move in once the first ones are gone.

treatments.name: Housekeeping advice
treatments.body: The firm points out what's drawing rodents in, such as open food, bins and clutter, so the problem doesn't return.

treatmentNote: Ask whether proofing is included or quoted separately, how many follow-up visits there are, and who removes trapped or dead rodents.
priceFactors: How many rodents there are, and how long they've been there.
The size and layout of the property, including ceiling spaces, storerooms and any garden.
How much proofing is needed, and what materials it takes.
The number of follow-up visits to check bait stations and traps.
Whether it's a one-off job or a regular service, which is common for offices and for landed homes near drains or greenery.
Access to ceiling spaces, roof eaves or service ducts.
prepare: Put food in sealed containers, and don't leave pet food or fruit out overnight.
Note where you've seen droppings or gnaw marks, or heard noises, and at what time.
Clear access to storerooms, under the sink, behind appliances and to the false-ceiling hatch if there is one.
Don't put down your own poison beforehand. Rodents that die in the ceiling or walls cause a lasting smell, and home products often aren't placed safely.
Tell the firm about children, pets and anyone vulnerable in the home, so bait and traps are placed to suit.
onTheDay: The firm inspects inside and out, including ceilings, drains and likely entry points.
Bait stations or traps are set along the routes the rodents are using.
Entry points are sealed, either on the day or on a later visit if materials are needed.
Before leaving, the firm sets dates to come back and check, and tells you what to watch for.
afterwards: Keep food sealed, bins closed and clutter down, and don't move the bait stations. If you notice a smell or fresh droppings after the firm's last visit, tell it: it may mean a gap was missed.

premises.hdb: In HDB flats, rodents usually come in from the ground floor or the refuse chute, or along pipes and cables, and often end up in the kitchen or a false ceiling. Treatment inside the flat goes together with sealing the gaps around pipes. If you see rats in the common areas, bin centre or void deck, report it to the town council, which looks after those areas.
premises.condo: In condos, rodents often move between units and common areas through service ducts and ceilings. Treat and proof your unit, and tell the managing agent, because the bin centre, car park and landscaping are the management corporation's to treat.
premises.landed: Landed homes have more ways in: drains, the garden, roof eaves, trees touching the roof and gaps around the kitchen and service yard. Proofing is usually a bigger part of the job, and landed homes near drains or greenery often keep a regular service.
premises.office: In offices, rodents are usually drawn by pantries, food waste and cabling in ceilings and raised floors, where gnawing can damage wiring. The firm can work out of hours and set up a regular inspection programme with records. If you lease the space, involve building management, because the source is often in shared areas.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get rid of rats?
faqs.a: It depends on how many there are and how they're getting in. Baiting and trapping usually run over several visits, and the job isn't finished until the entry points are sealed. The firm will set out its schedule in the quote.

faqs.q: Is rat bait safe with children and pets?
faqs.a: Firms put bait in locked, tamper-resistant stations to keep it out of reach, and use traps where bait isn't suitable. Tell the firm about children and pets when you book.

faqs.q: Why is there a smell after treatment?
faqs.a: A rodent that has eaten bait can die in a ceiling, wall or duct. The firm can usually help find and remove it, which is one reason proofing and follow-up visits matter.

name: Ants
metaDescription: Ant control in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices: why spraying can make some ants worse, how baiting works, what affects the price.
summary: Ant inspection and treatment for homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: A trail of ants to a spill is a nuisance you can wipe away. Ants that keep coming back, turn up in the bedroom or bathroom, or nest in walls, electrical sockets and plant pots need treatment that reaches the colony, and with some species the wrong spray makes the problem spread.
Tell us what you're seeing and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm. The firm identifies the ant, finds the nest and quotes the treatment.
signs: Trails of tiny ants along skirting, worktops and window frames, often leading to food, sugar or pet bowls.
Ants coming out of electrical sockets, switch plates, cracks between tiles or gaps in window frames, a sign they're nesting inside the wall.
Ants in bathrooms and bedrooms, well away from food, often after water.
Small heaps of soil or debris near walls, plant pots or garden beds.
Winged ants indoors, which can mean a mature colony nearby.
Stings or bites, especially from ants in the garden.
signsNote: Common household ants here include tiny pale ghost ants and pharaoh ants, fast, erratic crazy ants, and larger ants in gardens. The species decides the treatment, so a close-up photo helps.

treatments.name: Inspection and identification
treatments.body: The firm follows the trails to find where the ants are nesting and identifies the species, since the right treatment differs between them.

treatments.name: Baiting
treatments.body: Slow-acting bait gel or granules are carried by worker ants back to the nest, where they reach the queens. It's the main treatment for most indoor ants. It's slower than spraying, but it goes after the source.

treatments.name: Nest treatment
treatments.body: Where the nest can be reached, in a wall void, a plant pot or a garden bed, dust or liquid is applied directly to it.

treatments.name: Targeted perimeter treatment
treatments.body: For ants coming in from outside, a residual insecticide may be applied around doors, window frames and entry points. Firms choose this carefully indoors, because some species, such as pharaoh ants, react to repellent sprays by splitting into several new colonies.

treatments.name: Follow-up
treatments.body: A follow-up visit checks whether the bait has worked and tops it up wherever ants are still feeding.

treatmentNote: With baiting, activity drops over days rather than straight away. Ask the firm how long it expects before you see a difference, and what to do if you don't.
priceFactors: The species, and where the nest is.
How many rooms are affected, and whether the ants are also nesting outside.
The number of visits needed to clear the colony.
The size of the property, including gardens and planters at landed homes.
Whether it's a one-off treatment or part of a regular general pest service.
prepare: Stop spraying the ants in the days before treatment. It scatters them and can put them off the bait.
Wipe up food and sugary spills and keep food sealed, but leave the trails themselves so the firm can follow them.
Note where you see ants, and where they seem to disappear to.
Move things away from the skirting and cabinets where the trails run.
onTheDay: The firm follows the trails, identifies the species and looks for nests.
Bait is placed along the trails and near nests, and any nest it can reach is treated directly.
Entry points from outside may be treated with a residual product.
Before leaving, the firm tells you what not to disturb and when to expect results.
afterwards: You may see more ants on the bait for a day or two: that's the bait working, so don't wipe them away or spray them. Keep food sealed and fix any leaks, because many household ants are after water as much as food.

premises.hdb: In HDB flats, ants usually come in along pipes, window frames and cracks in the walls, sometimes from neighbouring units, and nest in walls, sockets and cabinets. Baiting inside the flat is the usual treatment.
premises.condo: In a condo, ants may be coming from the landscaping, planters on the balcony or a neighbouring unit. Treating your unit is yours to arrange; if the source is the common landscaping, tell the managing agent.
premises.landed: At landed homes, ants often nest outside, in the garden, planters and along the walls, and come in through doors and windows. Treatment usually covers the outside and the garden as well as indoors.
premises.office: In offices, ants gather in pantries, around desks where people eat and along cabling. Baiting can be done out of hours, and asking staff not to leave food at their desks helps it work faster.

faqs.q: Why do ants keep coming back after I spray them?
faqs.a: Sprays kill the ants you can see, but not the nest or the queens, which keep producing workers. With some species, spraying can also split the colony into several. Baiting reaches the nest instead.

faqs.q: Is ant bait safe for children and pets?
faqs.a: Bait is used in small amounts, in cracks and along trails, often inside stations. Tell the firm about children and pets so it can place the bait out of reach.

faqs.q: How long does ant treatment take to work?
faqs.a: Baiting usually shows results over several days, as workers carry the bait back to the nest. The firm will tell you what to expect and when any follow-up is due.

name: Mosquitoes
metaDescription: Mosquito control in Singapore for HDB flats, condos, landed homes and offices: finding breeding spots, misting and fogging, and what affects the price.
summary: Mosquito inspection, breeding-spot checks and treatment for homes and offices, carried out by a partner pest-control firm.
intro: In Singapore, mosquitoes are more than a nuisance: the Aedes mosquito spreads dengue, and it breeds in the small pools of clean, standing water found in and around homes. Control starts with finding and removing the places they breed, then treating the places they rest.
Tell us what you're dealing with and we'll pass it to a partner pest-control firm. The firm inspects for breeding spots, quotes, and carries out the treatment.
signs: Bites during the day, especially in the early morning and late afternoon. Aedes mosquitoes bite in daylight, unlike many other kinds.
Small black mosquitoes with white markings on the legs and body, resting in dark, cool spots such as under furniture, behind curtains and in cupboards.
Larvae, small wriggling 'worms', in standing water: flower-pot plates, vases, pails, roof gutters, drains, bamboo-pole holders, and water pooled on plastic sheets or in unused toilets.
Mosquitoes around the garden, balcony or planters, particularly after rain.
Several people in the household or office being bitten regularly.
signsNote: If anyone at home has a sudden fever or other symptoms after being bitten, see a doctor. Mosquito control deals with the insects, not the illness.

treatments.name: Breeding-spot inspection
treatments.body: The firm checks everywhere water can collect, indoors and out, and removes or treats it. This matters most, because treating adult mosquitoes doesn't stop new ones hatching.

treatments.name: Larviciding
treatments.body: Where standing water can't be removed, such as in drains, gully traps and gutters, a larvicide is applied to kill the larvae before they become adults.

treatments.name: Residual spraying
treatments.body: Insecticide is applied to walls, foliage and shaded spots where adult mosquitoes rest, so they're killed when they land.

treatments.name: Misting and thermal fogging
treatments.body: A fine mist or fog of insecticide knocks down adult mosquitoes in gardens, drains and outdoor areas. It acts fast but doesn't last, so it's used alongside removing breeding spots, not instead of it.

treatments.name: Regular service
treatments.body: For landed homes with gardens and for larger premises, firms often propose a regular programme of inspection and treatment.

treatmentNote: Ask what the firm will treat indoors and what outdoors, and how long to keep windows shut or stay out of treated areas.
priceFactors: The size of the property and its outdoor areas: gardens, planters, drains and roof gutters.
How many breeding spots there are, and how hard they are to reach.
The methods: an inspection alone, or with larviciding, residual spraying and fogging.
Whether it's a one-off treatment or a regular service.
Access to roof gutters, drains and other high or enclosed spots.
prepare: Do a round of the home first: turn over pails, empty flower-pot plates, change vase water, and clear any gutters and drains you can reach safely.
Tell the firm about ponds, fish tanks and pets, so it can keep them clear of the treatment.
Bring laundry, pet bowls and children's toys in from the outdoor areas to be treated.
If outdoor fogging is planned, close windows and doors and keep people and pets indoors while it's done.
onTheDay: The firm inspects indoors and outdoors for breeding spots and resting places.
Breeding spots are removed, or treated with larvicide where they can't be.
Resting areas get a residual spray, and outdoor areas may be misted or fogged.
Before leaving, the firm tells you how long to stay clear of treated areas, and what to check each week to stop breeding coming back.
afterwards: Treatment won't last if water keeps collecting. Check pails, plates, gutters and drains every week, and again after heavy rain.

premises.hdb: In HDB flats, the usual breeding spots are indoors and along the corridor: flower-pot plates, vases, pails, bamboo-pole holders and plants outside the door. Most flats need a thorough check for breeding spots and treatment of indoor resting places rather than fogging. The common-area drains and landscaping are the town council's to treat.
premises.condo: In a condo, check your balcony, planters and aircon ledge. The pools, landscaping and common drains are the management corporation's, so if mosquitoes seem to be coming from outside your unit, tell the managing agent.
premises.landed: Landed homes carry the most risk: gardens, roof gutters, drains, planters and outdoor items all collect water. Treatment usually covers the whole outdoor area, and many landed homes keep a regular programme.
premises.office: Offices usually have fewer breeding spots, but pantries, indoor plants, roof areas and nearby construction can create them. If you lease the space, building management normally handles the exterior and drains, so the firm works on your unit and anything you control.

faqs.q: Does fogging get rid of mosquitoes?
faqs.a: Fogging knocks down adult mosquitoes quickly, but it doesn't stop new ones hatching from water nearby, and the effect wears off. It works as part of a programme that removes breeding spots, not on its own.

faqs.q: Is mosquito treatment safe for pets and fish?
faqs.a: Tell the firm about pets, fish tanks and ponds before treatment. It can avoid or cover those areas, and tell you how long to keep pets indoors.

faqs.q: How often is mosquito treatment needed?
faqs.a: It depends on the property. A flat may need only a one-off check and treatment, plus your own weekly checks, while a landed home with a garden often benefits from a regular service. The firm will suggest how often after inspecting.
